record.body:
[DEFINITION] A preparatory step inside the path of a collection, run with Engagement.ps1 before the collection is read. It assesses each member surface in each verse it occurs in by the role it takes there (characteristic or qualifier, or, bearing on the finding, object, relational_target or enactment), and writes the assessment as observations with a node for each verse where the role holds; a surface judged to have no bearing in a verse is recorded as a silence whose node takes the role standalone, and a re-evaluation of the verse reconsiders it. The surface's group then follows from the roles: a characteristic in any verse makes it a behaviour, a qualifier in some verses and never a characteristic makes it an inner_being_state, and no inner-being role in any verse takes it out of the study group (cfg_setting engagement.group_rule). It is not the result of the study, and everything it assesses is inferential until the researcher confirms it.

[BACKGROUND] Behaviour rule 127 (the unit of study is the collection) names it as preparatory. Some surface judgements in surface_term carry the judge rule:engagement. The role of a no-bearing node is cfg_setting engagement.no_bearing_role (standalone; researcher ruling on #2525, 2026-11-21).

record.body:
[DEFINITION] The role of a word in a finding: what the word is for the finding an observation states, judged by reading the verse, for each occurrence, against the inner-being operation the verse carries. It is never taken from the cluster tag, the collection, the word's other occurrences or its usual part, so the same word can be a characteristic in one verse and a qualifier in another, and each role is its own observation applied by its nodes to the verses where it holds. On a node the roles are: characteristic (the word behaves as a characteristic of the inner being, and the finding is about it) and qualifier (it binds to a characteristic and gives it value or context in place: manner, measure, strengthening, ground, cause, object, setting or the negator of a refusal; the observation states what it gives, and the word has no account of its own from that verse), which are relevant to the inner being; object (what the act is directed at, or its content), relational_target (the party the act engages) and enactment (the outward act the inner act produces), which bear on the finding; standalone, which records that the word was read in the verse and holds nothing for the inner being (it binds to nothing, and it is a role and not an absence; see standalone); and lexical, which records that the word was read lexically and its inner-being role has not been assessed (cfg_setting reading.node_roles; behaviour rule 130). A party's role is an observation, not a field. A role is never a verdict: a verse is not closed as 'only a qualifier' or 'no bearing'.

[BACKGROUND] Held in ib_node.role, required on a node that names a word and not set on every node (11,926 of 68,426 live nodes on 2026-11-21, all written by earlier methods). The study's earlier method named three roles, characteristic, qualifier (or process-element) and standalone; the node adds object, relational_target, enactment and lexical. Two other columns are also called role and are not this one: verse_lexical.role holds the cluster codes of the word's Strong's code copied onto each occurrence, with no reading of the verse in it, and verse_span_index.role holds an older analytic role set by earlier campaigns, on part of the spans, with a vocabulary that grew by use. The role is also what the engagement step reads to set a surface's group (a characteristic in any verse makes the surface a behaviour, a qualifier only an inner-being state, no inner-being role in any verse takes it out of the study) and what the deeper reading is to be filtered on, which is not yet defined. This entry is in the contentious glossary: it stays a draft until the researcher settles it.
